findings.title: Null dereference on empty destinationCalendar when location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` is `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Any booking with location Google Meet whose organizer and event type have no destination calendar now throws a TypeError in `EventManager.create`, so the booking fails instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: `credentialId` is now `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so references created for video results are saved without a credentialId. `handleCancelBooking` only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set. Video meetings (Zoom, Daily, etc.) for new bookings will therefore not be deleted on cancellation. Keep `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results.

findings.title: Fallback calendar lookup is dead code; update falls back to undefined calendarId
findings.body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only evaluates the `find` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then compares against that falsy value, so it never matches. Previously the code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. For references without `externalCalendarId` (older bookings or the non-credential path), `calendars.events.update` is now called with `calendarId: undefined` and fails. The same dead lookup exists in `deleteEvent` (line ~317); that path still defaults to "primary", but the destination calendar is lost.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses possibly undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` can now be `undefined`. Insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credential, the patch that adds the Meet link to the description fails silently.

findings.title: Non-Google calendars always use the main host's calendar id for every host
findings.body: `createEvent` now runs once per host's destination calendar, but Office365 (and similarly Lark and CalDAV) always reads `destinationCalendar[0]`, which is the main host's calendar. For a second host it posts to `/me/calendars/<main host calendar id>/events` using the second host's token, and that request fails. The credentialId passed to `createEvent` is ignored. The multi-host fix therefore only works for Google Calendar.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent silently creates nothing for non-main hosts
findings.body: For a collective host whose CalDAV credential is not the main host's, the filter `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` matches none of that host's calendars. `Promise.all([])` resolves, so the method returns success while no event is created in the host's calendar.

findings.title: Lark createEvent ignores the target credential's destination calendar
findings.body: `createEvent` always uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, which is the main host's calendar. When a collective host with Lark is not the main host, the event and its attendees are created against another user's calendar id and the request fails.

findings.title: Team host calendars dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing, so the collective hosts' calendars are discarded. This is the exact multi-host scenario the PR is meant to fix. Initialize to `[]` or assign the team calendars when the base is null.

findings.title: loadUsers refactor drops organization select and changes error behavior
findings.body: The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { slug }`, so downstream code that reads the organizer's organization slug (e.g. building the org booker URL) gets undefined for dynamic group bookings. The refactor also throws on an empty `dynamicUserList`. Every non-HttpError/Prisma error is converted into a generic 500 "Unable to load users", which replaces the previous behavior. These changes are unrelated to the PR's purpose.

findings.title: Inverted slug condition for org creation
findings.body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which sets the slug immediately only when billing is disabled. The new code sets it only when billing IS enabled. With billing enabled the org gets its slug before payment, bypassing the requestedSlug flow. With billing disabled (self-hosted) the org is created without a slug. This unrelated change inverts behavior.

findings.title: Only the first old calendar event is deleted when merging on reschedule
findings.body: With multiple calendar references per booking (one per collective host), the `newBookingId` path still uses `booking.references.find(...)`, so only the first host's old calendar event is deleted. The other hosts keep stale events in their calendars.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation repeated per reference and ignores other hosts
findings.body: The recurring branch now runs inside the per-reference loop, so the full deletion pass over all of the organizer's calendar credentials repeats once per calendar reference. Each pass uses only the organizer's credentials and only the first `_calendar` reference of each booking. Other collective hosts' recurring events are never deleted, while the organizer's events receive redundant delete calls.

findings.title: Webhook payload shape of destinationCalendar changed to array
findings.body: `CalendarEvent` is spread directly into webhook payloads, so `destinationCalendar` changes from an object (or null) to an array, or `[]`. External webhook consumers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` will break. The e2e test was updated to expect `[]` without any documentation or migration note for this public contract change.
